newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks made headway on bad loan problem - Fed.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks made headway on bad loan problem - Fed.

text.p: Japanese banks have made significant progress in resolving their bad loan problems over the past several years, but there are still important challenges for those operating internationally, a U.S. Federal Reserve official said on Monday.

"While significant progress has been made, I think an important challenge has remained," Chester Feldberg, executive vice president at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, said at a symposium in Tokyo.

He said Japanese banks need to further strengthen their capital. Japanese banks have been able to maintain a minimum capital-to-assets ratio of eight percent required under rules set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
